restrictions: Generic memoryless Pollard-rho (Floyd) on f(x)=H(enc32(x)), H the complete blake3-r3-prefix-v1 hash (exactly three prefix rounds in every compression), enc32 the 32-byte little-endian encoding; each evaluation is one root compression of a single 32-byte chunk.
At most 5*2^128 compressions plus <=64 word ops per compression at 1/638 each: T < 2^130.46.
Memory < 2^16 bytes (state, tortoise/hare, code). No tables, preprocessing or advice.
Success >= 0.3934 - 2^-128 under heuristic H_random (random-mapping first-repeat distribution).

heuristics.statement: Let x0 be uniform random and x_{i+1}=f(x_i). Let L be the number of distinct values before the first repeat. Assume Pr[L<=2^128] >= 1-exp(-(1-2^-128)/2) and Pr[mu=0 and L<=2^128] <= 2^-128 as for a uniform random mapping. Then success >= 0.3934 - 2^-128 > 0.39 (proof.md).
heuristics.scope: One trajectory of the full-width map f on 2^256 points from a fresh uniform start, complete three-round BLAKE3 on 32-byte messages.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer experiment rho-reduced runs the same Floyd algorithm on the 16-bit truncation of f; organizer checks digest bits 0..15 agree on returned distinct messages. Locally 40/40 successes, mean ~800 evaluations. Extrapolated to 256 bits. Three-round BLAKE3 has full diffusion after the first round and no published practical collision for the complete hash at this length; no known structure that would make the first-repeat distribution substantially worse than random.
heuristics.limitations: Assumption, not proved for three-round BLAKE3. Experiment is 16-bit only; no 256-bit witness. Generic attack.
